one_line: Classical Sanskrit physician who systematised diagnostic medicine in the Madhava Nidanam (c. 700–800 CE).

appearance.age_look: early 40s, lean scholar’s build with calm posture
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed mustache and short beard line along the jaw, thoughtful almond-shaped eyes with a focused gaze, default expression gentle but intensely observant, like he is quietly assessing a patient
appearance.hair: black hair parted at the center and combed back into a short, tidy topknot at the back of the crown; front kept smooth without loose strands; simple narrow cream-coloured cloth headband tied around the topknot base, no ornate crown
appearance.costume: He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton angarakha (wrap tunic) crossing left over right and tied with thin fabric ties, the neckline modest and V-shaped; over this, a soft ochre-yellow cotton uttariya (shawl) draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back, with a thin maroon border; his lower garment is a plain ankle-length dhoti in muted cream, wrapped and pleated at the front in a Deccan-style tuck, revealing simple brown leather sandals; around his neck is a single strand of small rudraksha-style beads, and at his right wrist a plain copper bangle; the overall look is that of a wandering but respected medical teacher, practical and uncluttered.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript bound with a maroon cord in his left hand, with a simple wooden diagnostic kit pouch hanging at his waist—containing a small bronze urine-collection bowl and a thin wooden tongue depressor—though the manuscript is the clear primary prop he carries.

ref_desc: Madhavakara is a lean, medium-brown man in his early 40s with a short black topknot and cream headband, off-white angarakha, cream dhoti, ochre shawl with maroon border, simple beads and copper bangle, holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript and small diagnostic kit in off-white, ochre, maroon and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw Madhavakara as an anime-style full-body character: a lean, early-40s Sanskrit physician with an oval, medium-brown face, focused almond eyes, straight nose, neat mustache and short jawline beard, black hair tied in a tidy short topknot at the crown wrapped with a narrow cream cloth headband. He wears an off-white long-sleeved angarakha tunic crossing left over right, modest V-neck, reaching to the knee, over a plain cream ankle-length dhoti wrapped and pleated in a practical Deccan style. A soft ochre-yellow shawl with a thin maroon border drapes from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back. His feet are in simple brown leather sandals. Add a single strand of small bead necklace at his neck and a plain copper bangle on his right wrist. In his left hand he firmly holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bound with a maroon cord, and at his waist hangs a small, subtle diagnostic kit pouch hinting at a bronze bowl and wooden tongue depressor, but keep the manuscript as the clear signature prop. Use a palette dominated by off-white, ochre yellow, maroon, cream and brown, and present him front-facing with clear visibility of his face, hair, costume details and the manuscript for a clean model sheet style pose.
